text:
Situation: Oxytocin is not on FDA's current shortage list as of 2026-10-21. The prior shortage was first posted 2022-09-23 and has since been resolved. Current inventory across Corvale East and Corvale General ranges from 7.6 to 16.5 days of supply for the two oxytocin presentations.

Why (FDA record): FDA's records show oxytocin is not on the current shortage list as of 2026-10-21; the prior shortage was first posted 2022-09-23 and has since been resolved. The prior shortage posting followed FDA inspections at Fresenius Kabi USA LLC (FEI 1450022) that ended 2020-05-18 and 2022-06-30, both classified OAI, 858 and 85 days before the 2022-09-23 posting. A later inspection at the same plant ended 2023-08-24 and was classified VAI, 335 days after the shortage posting. A second Fresenius Kabi plant (FEI 3001833549) had an inspection ending 2023-10-13 classified VAI, 385 days after the posting.

Our position: Supply is limited but not in shortage per FDA. Two P&T-approved alternative manufacturers are available. The preferred alternative is oxytocin 10 units/mL from Par Health USA, LLC (NDC 42023011602), approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2026-04-16. A secondary option is oxytocin 10 USP units/mL from Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC (NDC 63323001210), approved by Riley Brooks, PharmD on 2026-01-24. Both require dose and volume recalculation and pharmacist verification. A third option from West-Ward Pharmaceuticals Corp is not on FDA's shortage list today, but its label names no plant we could place.

Recommended actions:
1. Continue current oxytocin allocations while monitoring daily usage; buyer to manage.
2. Activate Par Health USA, LLC product as primary alternative per P&T preference; pharmacist to verify each order.
3. Maintain Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC product as secondary alternative; pharmacist to verify each order.
4. Evaluate West-Ward Pharmaceuticals Corp only if options 1-3 are unavailable; buyer to approve purchase.
5. Report inventory trends to P&T committee weekly; buyer to prepare report.

Not recommended: Do not initiate new shortage protocols or restrict clinical use based on shortage status, as FDA records show no active shortage.
